why: Intro to Git and GitHub plan (docs/ui-next/catalog/plans/intro-git.json), 'Stage and commit'. The learner chained the two commands with && and misspelled the file: `git add pancake.md && git commit -m "Add pancakes"`. git add failed ('fatal: pathspec 'pancake.md' did not match any files'), so && never ran the commit. `git status` says 'No commits yet' with pancakes.md untracked. 'Add pancakes' and 'pancakes.md' are on screen only in the typed command and the untracked list.

step.title: Commit pancakes.md
step.instructions: Stage pancakes.md with git add pancakes.md, then commit it with git commit -m "Add pancakes". git log --oneline should show one commit.

files.cookbook/pancakes.md:
# Pancakes

- 1 cup flour
- 1 cup milk
- 2 eggs
- pinch of salt

Terminal: tripi@mac cookbook % git add pancake.md && git commit -m "Add pancakes"
fatal: pathspec 'pancake.md' did not match any files
(use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)
